title: Add Entry-Price Guard on GPU Engine

findings.title: No new unit test added for the new guard on GPU engine
findings.detail: The CPU engine has a sibling test `test_invalid_entry_price_raises` at tests/unit/test_cpu_engine.py:1003 that exercises the exact same guard (zero entry price). The GPU engine change introduces an identical guard at gpu_fuzzy_trader/backtest/gpu_engine.py:643-651 but ships no corresponding test in tests/unit/test_gpu_engine.py. The implementer reports '146 passed' but no new test was added. Other ValueError paths on the GPU engine (e.g., `test_missing_feature_raises_clear_error` line 396, chromosome-width line 553) are explicitly covered, so the asymmetry is inconsistent with the file's existing testing pattern.
findings.fix: Add a test in tests/unit/test_gpu_engine.py mirroring tests/unit/test_cpu_engine.py:1003-1007. Suggested body: build a small DataFrame with `label_open_next = [100.0, 0.0, 100.0]` (zero entry price is invalid) and assert `pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Invalid label_open_next")` on `GPUBacktestEngine(...)` construction. Optionally also cover NaN and negative cases to lock in edge-case behavior.

correctness_review.verification: Side-by-side comparison of cpu_engine.py:493-501 and gpu_engine.py:643-651 confirms identical logic: `invalid_mask = (~np.isfinite(entry)) | (entry <= 0)`, same `bad = int(np.sum(invalid_mask))` counter, same error message string 'Invalid label_open_next values (must be finite and positive). Bad rows: {bad}'.
correctness_review.placement_note: Guard inserted immediately after `entry = df['label_open_next'].values.astype(...)` (line 640) and before the first division-by-entry at `self._max_ret_jax = jnp.array((df['label_max_288'].values - entry) / entry * 100.0, ...)` (line 642). This matches the CPU engine placement and ensures degenerate entry prices are rejected before any downstream calculation.

edge_case_review.nan: caught — `np.isfinite(nan)` is False, so `~np.isfinite(entry)` is True
edge_case_review.inf: caught — `np.isfinite(inf)` is False, so `~np.isfinite(entry)` is True (covers both +inf and -inf)
edge_case_review.negative: caught — `entry <= 0` is True for any negative value
edge_case_review.empty_array: covered — `np.any(empty_mask)` is False, no exception raised (matches CPU engine behavior)

verified_manually.logic_correctness: Ran a 6-element array containing [100.0, 0.0, nan, 50.0, -10.0, inf] through the validation expression; correctly identified 4 bad rows and produced the expected error message. The 'all valid' case produced no false positives.
verified_manually.existing_tests: PYTEST_LOW_MEMORY=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_gpu_engine.py tests/unit/test_cpu_engine.py -k 'label_open_next or invalid_entry' -q → 1 passed (existing CPU test still green). Full gpu/cpu suite reported 146 passed in implementer handoff.

security_review: None expected — pure input validation. No I/O, no logging of untrusted data, no mutation of inputs.

maintainability_review.error_message_clarity: Good — message names the offending column, the required property ('finite and positive'), and the count of bad rows. This is sufficient for debugging a polluted `label_open_next` series without leaking raw data.
maintainability_review.code_style: Matches surrounding code style (no docstring on the guard block, consistent with cpu_engine.py). The blank line on either side of the block separates it from the `entry = ...` line and the `_max_ret_jax` assignment cleanly.
maintainability_review.duplication: Acceptable — the CPU and GPU engines each carry their own validation by design (they are independent code paths with separate pre-extraction blocks). Extracting to a shared helper would be a separate refactor and is out of scope for this task.

out_of_scope_changes: None. Single-file, 9-line insertion with no incidental edits.
summary: Implementation is correct, well-placed, and a faithful port of the CPU engine guard. Edge cases (nan/inf/zero/negative) are all covered by the same single expression. Only issue is a minor test-coverage gap: the new guard is not exercised by a GPU-engine unit test, breaking symmetry with the existing CPU-engine test for the same logic.
